observations: The native-vector approach keeps the exact source contour graph, quadratic curve types and all original short-stroke contours; unlike raster reconstruction it does not rebuild outlines as polygons.

Pure vector flex accepts15/16 sample glyphs under per-glyph geometry guards and makes long strokes less mechanically straight. Whole Khitan/Tangut fields pass at384px; Jigmo2/3 fields fail and must not be adopted.

Contour-normal width normalization plus low-frequency flex and rounded native line corners reduces mechanical edge character. Guard reductions preserve counters but often suppress the visually useful normalization.
Stronger near-monoline normalization preserves whole Khitan and Tangut samples at384px, but Tangut retreats to .25 strength. Jigmo2/3 whole fields fail despite individual glyph acceptance.
At22px dominant thin-horizontal/thick-vertical serif construction still remains for sampled Tangut and rare Han. None of these candidates establishes complete approved dense comic styling.

Native Seal Sans sampled in output/font-review/cubic-pressure/comparison.png already has tapered stroke starts and flowing variable width. Provisional native retention protects sign identity and is appropriate for this bounded sample; .35 pressure is too subtle to count as new style adaptation.

boundedProductionStrategy: Treat source categories separately: native calligraphic seal may retain ink; Khitan needs native stacked layout with bounded curve flex; Tangut/rare Han need serif-contrast treatment, not generic edge noise.

Before production, run8–16 representative complete clusters per dense source, including small counters and shortest detached strokes, with a single common viewport at1024 and384px and actual22/44px visual specimens.

Choose optical-finer-ink candidates only where the authoritative native form survives and style visibly improves. Do not raise normalization strength until a source passes both per-glyph and whole-field guards.

Cache by source hash, glyph outline hash, and treatment constants. Process only routed contributing glyphs in bounded groups. Preserve all native GSUB/GPOS/GDEF/hmtx and hint/layout metadata deliberately; invalidate dependent CJK/variant assets only after accepted group builds.

For failed rare Han, a better next implementation is native contour-pair stroke correspondence with local feature-size constraints: normalize wide vertical stems and round terminal serifs while keeping each short native stroke and counter. The current nearest-skeleton normal estimate is too conservative or unsafe and should not be mass applied.
Refresh licences, derivative names, source offers where relevant, manifests and coverage only after a production candidate is accepted. These experiments do not authorize or require a mass rebuild.
limitations: No browser calls were used. All rendered specimens use local native outlines/HarfBuzz/PyMuPDF.
Local contour/raster guards are geometry checks, not proof of linguistic identity or arbitrary expression correctness.
No production font, manifest, B-owned input, licence or source-offer file was modified in this task.
The first dense-pen output predates added skeleton-protection; its PNG/JSON are saved but the current dense_pen.py implements the protected trial. Vector variants remain separately reproducible.
